reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes OneCoin as an opportunity to obtain cryptocurrency and potentially make Bitcoin-like money, while presenting audits and a large member count as reassurance that it is legitimate. The video directs viewers toward participation through a sign-up page and repeatedly asks them to contact the speaker, including a displayed phone number. These assurances and recruitment prompts encourage viewers to join despite the lack of substantiated evidence in the supplied content for the claimed value or legitimacy.

citations.quote: Well here's a chance to take advantage of that same error now with the company called one coin now.
so is one coin a scam well i guess not according to what all the records are showing now i want to show you something real quick there is 485 000 people who has joined this trend already
if you would like to talk more about this then simply contact me at the number that's on the screen

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker raises the central objection directly: “is this a scam” (ASR_0001), then gives a qualified answer, “i guess not according to what all the records are showing” (ASR_0002). That wording matters. He presents a conclusion tied to what he says the records show, not a promise that participation is risk-free or profitable. The question remains visible in the title as well (TITLE_0001). A favorable answer to a scam question should not, by itself, be treated as proof of deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: is this a scam
i guess not according to what all the records are showing
Onecoin Scam Is Onecoin a big scam

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that the speaker compares the opportunity with Bitcoin, but its quoted phrase says “here's a chance,” not that anyone will earn a particular return (ASR_0001). Its contact quote offers a conversation (ASR_0002); it does not establish what a caller would be asked to pay. The speaker's qualified conclusion should be assessed as his stated opinion about the records, not converted into an unconditional guarantee (ASR_0002).

citations.quote: Well here's a chance to take advantage of that same error now with the company called one coin now.
if you would like to talk more about this then simply contact me at the number that's on the screen
i guess not according to what all the records are showing

true_side_reply.rebuttal: “I guess” does not neutralize the pitch around it. The speaker tells viewers who missed Bitcoin about people who “made millions overnight” and immediately calls OneCoin a chance to take advantage of that same era (ASR_0001). The displayed “Become A Member” and “Sign up” pathway (F0042) makes the reassurance part of an invitation to participate, even without an explicit guaranteed return.

citations.quote: you've heard about those guys who made millions overnight when they sold their little bit coins. Well here's a chance to take advantage of that same error now with the company called one coin now.

opening.argument: Judge, this is also a walk-through of the speaker's reasons for evaluating OneCoin. He introduces the question “is this a scam” (ASR_0001), discusses a claimed monthly blockchain audit (ASR_0001), and explains his understanding of how the coins are mined (ASR_0002). The page shown under “Is This A Scam?” presents audit material and an interview for viewers to inspect (F0017). Those are features of an examination of a cryptocurrency operation. The material may be one-sided, but showing the basis for a favorable assessment is different from demonstrating that viewers are being deceived.

citations.quote: is this a scam
one coin has hired Cylper Ford is to come on and audit their Blockchain each and every month
dr. Rusia has figured out a system where it allows you to mine these coins

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the audit discussion as mere reassurance, but the speaker identifies a specific proposition for viewers to consider: a company auditing the blockchain monthly (ASR_0001). The visible page supplies related material (F0017). Neither proves the audit claim is true, but the supplied record does not establish it is false either. A favorable, imperfect review can contain an invitation to follow up without ceasing to be commentary.

citations.quote: one coin has hired Cylper Ford is to come on and audit their Blockchain each and every month

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The opening describes the speaker's claims, not independent verification of them. More importantly, the explanation serves an overt pitch: he calls OneCoin a chance to repeat the Bitcoin opportunity (ASR_0001), while the site displays a “Sign up” button beside its membership count (F0042). The audit page (F0017) does not establish coin value, realizable gains, or the legitimacy of that invitation.

citations.quote: Well here's a chance to take advantage of that same error now with the company called one coin now.

opening.argument: Judge, distinguish an invitation to learn about membership from an established loss mechanism. The page does invite visitors to “Become A Member” and “Sign up” (F0042), and the speaker offers to talk with interested viewers (ASR_0002). But the cited material does not show a required deposit, promised payout schedule, request for credentials, or downline-income terms. He describes mining coins and their possible uses (ASR_0002), which can be read as a pitch for a business offering. The presence of promotion should not alone settle whether the offer shown is a scam.

citations.quote: if you would like to talk more about this then simply contact me at the number that's on the screen
it allows you to mine these coins then it's one of the things that people want to come and jump on because there is a lot of things you can do with your cryptocurrency

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution points to the sign-up page (F0042) and phone invitation (ASR_0002), but neither shows a viewer actually transferring money or receiving a promised return. Its member-count point is likewise a claim about participation, not evidence of a payout obligation (ASR_0002). Those omissions matter when deciding whether the observed promotion itself establishes the alleged financial mechanism.

citations.quote: if you would like to talk more about this then simply contact me at the number that's on the screen
there is 485 000 people who has joined this trend already

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The case does not depend on seeing a completed payment. The speaker first evokes Bitcoin holders who “made millions overnight,” then offers OneCoin as a comparable chance (ASR_0001). The site invites viewers to become members (F0042), and he asks them to contact him so they do not “miss out on the cryptocurrency era” (ASR_0002). The missing transaction details do not erase that recruitment pitch or substantiate its implied financial upside.
